children: U.S. natural gas futures post-back-to-back gains, rising2.2% to $2.959/mmBtu. Weather likely had little to do with the advance, although forecasts have turned a bit cooler since the start of the week, NatGasWeather.com says in a note. "Buying is likely due to politics/geopolitics as oil prices plunge due to Democrats winning the House and Senate to suggest the U.S.-Iran conflict will take on a more peaceful approach." Thursday's storage report is expected to show an 81 Bcf build for last week, according to a WSJ survey of analysts. That would increase the inventory surplus over the five-year average to 58 Bcf from 38 Bcf the week before. (anthony.harrup@wsj.com)
